output:
**Subject:** Papa's building. Please call me

Denis,

I tried to write this email four times. The first ones were half French, half insults, and not something a brother should send. If this one still sounds hard, you know why.

I will say it plainly: I am furious with you. But I am also writing because you are my brother and I don't want to lose you over this, so please read until the end.

Thursday, 6 in the morning, I am in the bakery shaping baguettes. A man with a camera walks in. He is from the agency. He tells me "Mr. Denis said you were okay with it." I did not know what he was talking about. Karine had to take me aside and calm me down. Then I went online and I found the listing on Centris, $1,150,000. Papa's building. I learned it from a stranger and a website, Denis. Not from my brother.

After maman's funeral you called me and you said, "No rush, we decide together." I kept those words. Together. And then you went to an agent and put it on the market, and you did not even pick up the phone. You let an agent, and then a photographer, tell me. I don't understand how you could do that to me. I really don't.

I know you live in Calgary, and your life is there, and maybe a building in Montreal is a weight for you. I can understand that. If you had called me and said, "I want out," I would have been hurt, but we could have talked like two brothers. That is all I needed from you.

And you knew what I wanted. In September I told you by phone that I wanted to buy your half. I told you the caisse had pre-approved me for $410,000. So this is not a surprise, it is not something I hid. You knew, and you listed it anyway.

I also want to say something, because I know you think I am being sentimental. Maybe a little, yes. It is papa's building, and I cannot hide that. But this is also business, and it is my whole living.

- Papa bought the building in 1979. My bakery has been downstairs for 31 years.
- I pay $2,400 a month to the estate. I was never late, not once.
- In 2019 I paid for the new roof myself, $38,000.
- I have 6 employees who depend on me, and 31 years of clients who know where to find us.
- My lease ends on April 30, 2027.

If a developer buys it, he will tear it down or make condos. And if he keeps the ground floor, he will double my rent. I cannot survive that. The bakery is not something I can pick up and move to another street. The people come to that corner because we have been there since before some of them were born. If the building goes, the bakery goes, and six people lose their jobs with it.

Do you remember when we were kids and papa let you sleep in the flour sack room at the back? You loved it. You were so proud of that room. I think about this a lot this week. For us this place was never just a listing with a price. It is where we grew up.

So this is what I am asking you.

First, take the building off the market this week. By Friday, if you can. Tell the agent to stop, no more photos, no more visits.

If you really cannot do that, then at least give me the first right to buy, in writing, before anything else is done. Let me try to buy your half, and let us sit down together and find how to make it work. I am ready to talk seriously, with numbers, with whatever you need to feel it is fair. I am not asking you for a gift. I am asking for a chance.

And I want an answer from you by phone. Not a text, and not a message from your wife. I know she reads English better than you, and I am sure she will read this with you, and I have nothing against her. But this is between you and me, two sons of the same father, and I want to hear your voice. Call me when you have read this. Any hour, I am up at 4 anyway.

I don't hate you, Denis. I want to be very clear about that. But I am angry, and I am hurt, and I want you to feel how much, because I think you did not understand it when you signed that paper. I am still your brother and I am still angry. Both are true at the same time.

Please call me.

[Your name]

---

Two things before you send:

- **The numbers.** Half of $1,150,000 is $575,000, and your pre-approval is $410,000. Denis or his agent may notice that gap right away. The email says you're ready to talk about how to make it work, which leaves room, but you might want to know before the call how you'd bridge it (an appraisal, a payment plan, a partner).
- **Your name and the deadline.** I left a placeholder for your name. "By Friday" assumes you send it today or tomorrow, so change it if that doesn't fit.
